title: Pricing Defects in Evaluation Environments by Expected Loss: A Probe Battery, the Floor It Had to Beat, and Twelve of Its Own Claims That Broke
description: Reinforcement-learning environments and eval suites are used on the strength of a verifier nobody re-checks. Assay is a battery of probes, 16 defect classes in all, that executes an environment and prices each missed defect and each false alarm under a stated cost profile. The arm it had to beat is the trivial one, flag_everything. On 33 environments with 54 planted defects, Assay has an expected loss of 57.0 (95% CI 8-142) against 474.0 (453-492) for the floor, a saving of 417.0 (330-471), and the saving separates in all four cost profiles. It reads larger than it is, and 285.0 is the figure to carry. 27.8% of the floor's loss is paid on 4 defect classes planted in no environment, and 25 of the 33 environments were written by the author. On the 8 third-party environments the saving is 76.0 with an interval that crosses zero (-4 to 121), and under one of the four profiles Assay loses to the floor there. Precision is 0.757: 17 false alarms, 14 of them on environments with no planted defect. A language-model gate that withholds the false alarms on environments with no correct answer deleted two real defects in 1 of 7 identical runs, so its mean saving over the deterministic arm is 2.4 against a median of 14.0. Against defects an independent team confirmed in tau2-bench, the recall of 0.339 is indistinguishable from random flagging (p=0.486). The repository broke 12 of its own published claims under its own red team and has published 22 retractions. The code is Apache-2.0. The deterministic arms reproduce without a GPU or an API key; the language-model arms and the gate do not. Not peer reviewed. Code, registrations and artifacts: https://github.com/caiotheodoro/assay
